correctness.rationale: I checked the all-length proof in RESULT.md:30–80. Every occurrence avoiding the proposed marks lies inside one of the listed gaps. For c≥a the two kinds of mixed gap factors 0^i1^j and 1^i0^j relocate across the right and left boundaries of the central run, respectively. For c<a and b=1 the only mixed gap factors are 10^i, which relocate to the selected second 1. For c<a and b≥2 the sole potentially mixed gap is 0^(c−1)1^(b−1), and its mixed factors relocate to the first boundary. The selected runs accommodate all pure gap factors, including when a gap is empty. For necessity in the third case, 0^a1 and 10^a must cross the outer boundaries, while 1^(b−1)0^c1 must cross both central boundaries. Their unique intervals [0,a], [a+1,a+b+c], [a+2b+c−1,2a+2b+c−1] are disjoint also at b=2. In every case the two single letters require two different positions. The substitution c=1+r, a=c+1+t, b=2+s is bijective and yields length 9+3r+2s+2t, proving the exceptional generating function and the two shortest exceptions. Comparing the order-three poles at 1 gives leading coefficients 1/6 and 1/2 there; all other poles give O(n) coefficients. Hence the density is 1/3.
residual_risks: The frozen script outputs report bounded checks only (216 exhaustive triples, 305 witness cases, generating coefficients through length 110). The code was inspected, not run for this review; correctness rests on the independently checked proof. The exhaustive checker stops at the first successful pair in the regime where a pair exists.

value.rationale: This gives a complete boundary, with optimal certificates, for an unbounded natural family of binary palindromes. It identifies exactly when three disjoint compulsory factors defeat a two-position attractor. The density is a useful consequence, not the sole contribution.
residual_risks: No claim for arbitrary five-run words or for all optimal position sets.
